subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the value of cos²52½° − sin²22½°.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply the cos² − sin² identity
steps.margin_note: First mark. cos²A − sin²B = cos(A+B)cos(A−B). The halves add and subtract cleanly: 52½ + 22½ = 75 and 52½ − 22½ = 30.
steps.memory_tip: cos²A − sin²B = cos(A+B)cos(A−B). The halves add and subtract cleanly to 75° and 30°.

recall.must_convey: That cos²A − sin²B = cos(A+B)cos(A−B) is applied, giving cos75° cos30°.
accept: use cos squared minus sin squared equals cos of the sum times cos of the difference giving cos seventy five cos thirty
the halves add to seventy five and subtract to thirty
apply the identity to get cos seventy five cos thirty
identity apply cheste cos seventy five cos thirty vasthundi
the sum and difference are seventy five and thirty

steps.why: This identity mixes a cosine squared with a sine squared, unlike the previous question — so no conversion is needed first, only the right formula.
common_mistakes: Converting one term and then using the wrong identity.

steps.label: Substitute the exact values
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cos75° = (√3 − 1)/(2√2) and cos30° = √3/2. Multiply and simplify.
steps.memory_tip: cos75° = (√3 − 1)/(2√2) and cos30° = √3/2. Multiply and simplify.

recall.must_convey: That the exact values are substituted and multiplied to give (3 − √3)/(4√2).
accept: cos seventy five is root three minus one over two root two and cos thirty is root three over two
multiply the two exact values to get three minus root three over four root two
the answer is three minus root three over four root two
rendu values multiply cheste three minus root three by four root two

steps.why: Multiplying √3 into (√3 − 1) gives 3 − √3, since √3 × √3 is 3. That is the only real simplification in the line.
common_mistakes: Rationalising unnecessarily and making an error.

insider_note: The identity here is cos²A − sin²B = cos(A+B)cos(A−B), with cosine on the left — not the sin² version. The half-degrees combine neatly into 75° and 30°.
